content:
Took me some time that the blue step was to lay it down.
At first I thought you gotta drill your own hole.
I found the square slot on the uni-wrench slots perfectly between the main body and the raised notch to help assist with holding the hinge base in place when securing
I feel like prusa gave up on the awesome embedded nut idea and opted to really make us work for it by providing parts that you make your own threads on... Come on

replies.content: My hands are so tired...not sure this was worth the work anymore. My previous experiences were so much better than this. I'm confident I wouldn't do this if I knew it would be this bad.

content:
Bad layout of photos.

1. Pre tap these with the screws.
2. Put screw in the hole and SLOWLY and CAREFULLY rotate the hinge until its taught. 
3. Align to correct position the give it one last 1/8 turn or so.

turning the hinge-base on to the screw while holding the screw tight the majority of the time works pretty fast, if couple turns left, place the hinge correctly and secure it from the underside till everything is tight
Pfff, this is a terrible one, I broke one of the hinge while trying to screw them in from the inside, but the lack of clearing and the self tapping screws make it really difficult.

There is not enough clearance between the top of the printer and the XY gantry to install self-tapping screws. 
The Hinge-bases need to be re-designed to use a M3nS insert instead of self-tapping holes.
The pictures of this make it seem like you are supposed to have the item standing up and drill the hole into the bottom as it stands like an upside down L... please update this...
Thread the screws into the part first before attempting to install them.

replies.content: Pre thread the parts.   I did it twice.   Then put the bolt in, hold it with the wrench abd spin the part down on the bolt.  When it becomes snug, position the hinge and final tighten from underneath,   Makes it much easier.

content: This is horrendous. I managed to make it more tolerable by holding the torx bit and spinning the hinge. This portion really needs a redesign.

replies.content: this and pre-threading the screws into the part worked a lot better

content: Why do we have to screw into plastic here? This is a part we might have to remove for maintenance and it would've been trivial to find a better solution. Also, why is there nothing to keep the part in correct orientation? Please replace the part by a better one, this is an incredibly bad solution, and I say that after attaching the spool holder and tool mounts, which were fine in comparison.

replies.content:
This feels like a band-aid solution. Heat-set inserts would solve so many issues/difficulties /screws in plastic in this build.

I guess not everyone would have the necessary hardware, but it's really cheap.

content:
Second photo is misleading, it shows the hinge in wrong position.
Also the 2x12sT is too long and it almost protrudes the hinge all way through.
For black on black parts, I wish the manual would show orange parts instead for easier visibility.

Along with pre tapping, it also is easier to insert the screw fully through the printer hole, put your tool on it, and then turn the hinge base onto it like a nut instead of trying to turn the screw due to space.

Tip: Pre-Tap the screw before installation.
The screw takes a lot of force to properly secure it and is really hard to reach from inside the printer.
